evidence: The sport list edit page stores its root in 0x20114970 and clears it on destroy. Its builder registers the same callback for event code 4 with data 0 on completion, 1 on the delete control and 2 on the flag control. The callback reads both getters and processes those branches only when the event code equals 4.
scope: getter calls in the sport list-edit callback while its page root is active
limitations: Changing the action data to another valid branch can use an incompatible event target and corrupt list state. A different low-byte value skips all three branches, while changing the event code skips the common branch. These points do not intercept other sports editing paths. Shared-entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence. The data slot is a page-lifecycle indicator, not proof of all-thread quiescence; skipping a registration may make its control nonfunctional.
registration_evidence: On initial page creation, the edit-data allocation is saved at 0x20114978 before sub_0c58f178 constructs controls; the root is assigned to 0x20114970 only after the builder returns. Thus root-based active filtering would miss the initial callback registrations. The destroy function clears the root and frees/clears the edit-data slot. The three registration callsites pass event code 4 and user-data values 2, 1 and 0 respectively; they do not use the returned descriptor.
